body.statement: The fixed Gaussian grid experiment is exactly embedded by vertex controls in the score diffusion, and the strict extension from the regular-payoff results of Wager and Xu and Adusumilli holds: arbitrary predictable policies, zero-allocation faces, and the discontinuous closed-test terminal loss satisfy \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|\to0\), \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\) for every \(m\), and \(V_n\to V\). Moreover, for each \(\epsilon>0\) there are predictable finite-horizon policies whose scenario-risk vectors converge coordinatewise to that of an \(\epsilon\)-optimal diffusion control.
body.justification: It identifies the attainable local-power regret frontier for the fixed confirmatory test.
body.gap: Adusumilli's 2026 theorem gives subsequential allocation-process representations and Adusumilli's 2025 convergence theorem uses Hölder data; this theorem adds a discontinuous closure payoff and legal boundary atoms.
body.consumer: It converts a continuum recruitment solution into asymptotically valid finite-stage policies for interAdapt-style designs.
